title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1973-12-01
source: Master Soundboard Reels > PCM > DAT> CDR

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a late‑1973 behemoth, highlighted by a monster Uncle John’s Band jam, Jerry on fire, and Keith’s steady keyboards.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine soundboard source that delivers every instrument up front with superb clarity and a spacious soundstage. The show itself is remembered as an all‑time favorite – from the legendary “Clear the Aisles” banter to a 30‑minute Playin’ ~ UJB ~ Playin’ stretch, healthy Phil bass work, and Jerry’s blazing yet patient guitar. Overall the performance feels both historic and endlessly enjoyable.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise across multiple detailed reviews for both musical performance and audio fidelity; no significant criticisms noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with superb instrument separation; minimal hiss, no drop‑outs reported. Reviewers describe it as “up front,” “fantastic soundstage,” and “very good” sound quality.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Late‑fall 1973 set flows smoothly with long jam sections and tight transitions; energy stays high throughout, making it a standout night in an often overlooked run.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Jerry “on fire yet patient” and that his playing is right there in the Boston air.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is described as healthy with space‑filled feedback during Uncle John’s Band.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux called the "unsung hero" of the sandwich, providing steady keyboard work.
